title: ChatCompletions payload shaper for legacy OpenAI clients: streaming, tool-calls, and structured-output compatibility
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Some legacy customers and integration tests rely on the OpenAI Chat Completions (ChatCompletions) semantics and payload shapes. We must provide a compatibility shaper that accepts Redwood's unified internal message/stream formats and emits an OpenAI-compatible request/response surface for downstream clients and proxies.

Scope: Implement a request/response marshaler layer that: 1) translates incoming OpenAI ChatCompletions-style requests into Redwood's internal request model, preserving tool/function call hints and structured-output expectations; 2) transforms Redwood responses (including streaming deltas) into the OpenAI-compatible streaming chunks, ensuring function call sequences, final_choice details, and structured JSON outputs are faithfully represented; 3) provides a strict idempotency and sequence-numbering mechanism to make partial retry safe for clients; 4) emits granular telemetry for token-level delays, function call latency, and schema enforcement failures.

Non-goals: Full protocol-level compatibility for proprietary transport variants; supporting deprecated experimental streaming frames outside the OpenAI SSE model.

Design summary:
- Request path: map OpenAI's messages[] and functions[] into Redwood's Message + ToolHint fields. Preserve role/name/content and any function descriptors as ToolManifest entries. For compatibility, accept both string and structured system messages.
- Streaming path: our runtime produces events (token, logprobs, kv-cache-snapshots, object parse partials). The shaper will coalesce these into an OpenAI SSE sequence: 'data: {"id":...,"object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":...}] }' and finalize with the standard final chunk (role/content/finish_reason). For partial function calls, stream a sequence of deltas where 'delta' includes an incremental 'function_call' field until it is complete.
- Structured outputs: when Redwood returns structured JSON or a schema-enforced object, include compatibility hints: in streaming deltas include 'structured_output_fragment' and set 'finish_reason' to 'structured' where applicable; emit the final 'message' object with 'content' equal to the serialized JSON and add metadata in 'usage' or 'response_metadata' fields for downstream parsers.
- Tool / function calling: translate Redwood tool invocation events into the OpenAI two-stage pattern: streaming tool output fragments followed by a final 'tool_call' completion with name/arguments. If a tool invocation occurs server-side (internal), expose a 'tool_call' stub so clients that expect to re-run tools can surface the invocation.
- Idempotency & ordering: attach monotonic sequence numbers and a request-level session id to every SSE chunk. Chunks include 'seq' and 'sess' to allow clients and proxies to detect missing frames. The shaper must support replays for up to 30s after the first chunk.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for request mapping with: functions array, role/name edge cases, nested content blocks, and ambiguous system prompts.
- Integration test verifying SSE stream shape for: normal text completion; multi-turn function call streaming; structured-output fragmentation and reassembly; and abrupt runtime fallback where model variant substitution occurs mid-stream.
- Telemetry: emit the following tags to tracing/metrics: compatibility.shaper.request_mapping, compatibility.shaper.stream_chunk, compatibility.shaper.schema_violation.
- Backwards compatibility: no changes to existing hosted API paths; the shaper sits as a gateway for clients using /v1/chat/completions and is opt-in behind a feature flag.

Implementation plan (high-level tasks):
1) Build request deserializer that accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions JSON and converts to Redwood internal request (ENG task).
2) Implement SSE chunk encoder with sequence/session fields and delta composition rules.
3) Tool-call adapter: map Redwood tool invocation events to OpenAI function_call deltas; include a small state machine to emit 'tool_call' finalization frames.
4) Structured-output wrapper: fragment JSON outputs into SSE-safe deltas and emit final metadata.
5) Tests: unit + integration harness with a fake client that validates strict conformance to OpenAI SSE ordering and chunk shapes.
6) Metrics & tracing integration and opt-in feature flag behind 'oa_compat_gateway'.

API examples:
- Incoming (OpenAI-style):
  {
    "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
    "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"Call the math tool"}],
    "functions": [{"name":"math","description":"evaluate expressions","parameters":{}}],
    "stream": true
  }
- Outgoing chunk (SSE stubbed):
  data: {"id":"req-842159","object":"chat.completion.chunk","seq":1,"sess":"s-abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"role":"assistant"}}]}
  data: {"id":"req-842159","object":"chat.completion.chunk","seq":2,"sess":"s-abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"function_call":{"name":"math","arguments":"2+2"}}}]}
  data: {"id":"req-842159","object":"chat.completion.chunk","seq":3,"sess":"s-abc123","choices":[{"delta":{"function_call":{"arguments":"4"}}}],"finish_reason":"function_call"}

Rollout plan: feature-flag behind 'oa_compat_gateway'. Stage 1: internal dogfood on staging (1 week), Stage 2: opt-in alpha for select customers (2 weeks), Stage 3: enable-by-default for /v1/chat/completions for Hosted API (post alpha signoff). Canary traffic will validate chunk ordering under packet loss via a simulated proxy.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: clients relying on nonstandard SSE frames may break. Mitigation: offer a 'strict' mode that rejects nonconforming requests; add a compatibility mode that logs and normalizes variants.
- Risk: increased latency from additional shaping step. Mitigation: micro-benchmark with target extra-latency < 5ms per chunk and fall back to pass-through for high-throughput dedicated pools.

Acceptance sign-off: PM + Infra + SRE + Security must approve; include a short runbook for Stream partials reconciliation.
